jobs.title: Terminate two Cat5e cables to keystone jacks
jobs.task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link.
tools: 110-style punch-down tool (a small hand tool that pushes wire into a plastic slot and trims the end at the same time)
Keystone jack x2 (small snap-in network socket, T568B wiring, to match the color chart printed on its body)
Short Cat5e patch cord (a ready-made cable with plugs on both ends, any length 0.5–2 ft)
Cable tester (a two-piece device: plug one end of the finished link into the master unit, the other end into the remote unit, and watch the numbered LEDs flash in sequence 1–8)
jobs.escalated: User reports one of the connectors feels warm and smells burnt. Possible overheating or electrical fault on the low-voltage wiring.
jobs.stopped_at: Identify the two blue Cat5e cables

jobs.title: Terminate Cat5e cables to keystone jacks
jobs.task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link.
jobs.escalated: A connector in this enclosure was previously reported as warm and smelling burnt. Heat and a burning smell on any wiring — even low-voltage — indicate a possible fault (short circuit, damaged insulation, or an unexpected voltage source) that must be diagnosed and cleared by a licensed electrician before any further work is done here.
